classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish overlapping and disjoint card events, represent their regions and count each favourable card once.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

If a card is drawn at random from a pack of 52 playing cards, what is the probability that it will be:

children.label: a
children.prompt: a Heart or the Ace of Clubs?

answer.worked:
Let $H$ denote Hearts and $C$ the Ace of Clubs. These events are mutually exclusive: the Venn regions contain 13 Hearts, 1 Ace of Clubs and 38 other cards.

$$\begin{align*}P(H\cup C)&=\frac{13+1}{52}\\P(H\cup C)&=\frac{14}{52}\\P(H\cup C)&=\frac{7}{26}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded solution Venn diagram with disjoint events H (Hearts) and C (Ace of Clubs).
spec.mathematics: H contains 13 cards, C contains 1 card, and 38 cards lie outside both; total 52.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ denote Hearts and $A$ Aces. The Ace of Hearts belongs to both sets. The Venn regions contain $13-1=12$ Hearts only, 1 card in both, $4-1=3$ Aces only and $52-16=36$ cards outside both.

$$\begin{align*}P(H\cup A)&=\frac{12+1+3}{52}\\P(H\cup A)&=\frac{16}{52}\\P(H\cup A)&=\frac{4}{13}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded solution Venn diagram for Hearts and Aces, with the Ace of Hearts counted in the intersection.
spec.mathematics: Hearts only 12; both 1; Aces only 3; neither 36; total 52.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ denote Hearts and $D$ Diamonds. These suits are mutually exclusive. The Venn regions contain 13 Hearts, 13 Diamonds and 26 other cards.

$$\begin{align*}P(H\cup D)&=\frac{13+13}{52}\\P(H\cup D)&=\frac{26}{52}\\P(H\cup D)&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded solution Venn diagram with disjoint Heart and Diamond suits.
